title: Prostate MRI
what: Detailed images of the prostate in a magnetic field, usually with contrast dye. No radiation.
why: For a high PSA, before a biopsy, for monitoring, and to plan treatment.
duration: usually 30 to 45 minutes; the report in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: A pacemaker, defibrillator, or other implant with electronics
Metal in your body: joint replacements, plates, clips on blood vessels, or shrapnel
If you recently had a prostate biopsy. Say the date. The MRI is sometimes moved
Allergy to contrast dye, or kidney disease
If you are afraid of closed spaces. Your doctor will suggest ways to help

prepare.title: Bowel
prepare.text: Sometimes you are asked to use a small cleansing enema the evening before or in the morning. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for 3 to 4 hours.

prepare.title: Abstinence
prepare.text: Often 2 to 3 days without ejaculation is advised. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off everything metal: jewelry, watches, hair clips, piercings. Leave your phone and cards in the locker.

steps: You change and leave everything metal in the locker
You lie on the table, and a soft coil pad is placed over the area
Sometimes a medicine is given so the bowel moves less
The machine knocks loudly. You get headphones or earplugs
Lie still. Staff talk to you over an intercom
At the end, contrast is given into a vein
feel: It does not hurt, but it is loud and tight
Sometimes the area feels warm. That is normal
With contrast: a cool feeling in the vein
after: You can go back to your day right away
After contrast, drink more water, unless your doctor said otherwise
The report includes a risk score. Take it to your urologist
red_flags: After contrast: itching, a rash, a swollen face, or trouble breathing. Tell the staff right away or call emergency services

faq.a: No. The MRI helps decide if a biopsy is needed and where to take tissue from.

faq.q: Is a probe put into the rectum?
faq.a: Usually not. The coil is placed on your belly. Check with the clinic.

faq.q: Can I have an MRI with fillings and crowns?
faq.a: Yes. Fillings and regular crowns are no problem. Tell staff about implants and prostheses in advance, and they will check.

reminders.text: Prostate MRI tomorrow. Check if you need an enema. Do not eat for 3 to 4 hours before.
